hypothesis: H77V: Spectral mesh de-aliasing (sigma=36 px = 3.6 km) of rectilinear 3.5 km / 7.0 km MT/geodetic/seismic inversion grids (resolving IR-H77G-01) coupled with corrected across-valley tubular Hessian demagnetization troughs (resolving IR-H77G-02), antiparallel gravity-basement step concordance, road/BLM-mining-deconfounded 1 m LiDAR & 10 m 3DEP fluvial knickpoint-scarp interactions (resolving IR-H77G-03), 8-channel fold-visible SLOCO mechanics, and Kernel-Convolved Lagrangian-Priced Dinkelbach Submodular Cover (LDSA).
physical_mechanism: Ascending hydrothermal fluids (150-250 C) along blind and incipient Great Basin normal/transtensional fault conduits sulfidize/oxidize primary magnetite to pyrite/smectite/leucoxene (producing linear multi-scale RTP magnetic troughs rather than positive ridges) and argilize surface fault rock, while leaving (1) transient 10 m 3DEP fluvial knickpoint wavefronts across the footwall/hanging-wall block step, (2) antiparallel gravity-vs-basement-depth gradient concordance, (3) regional 3.6 km de-aliased smectite clay-cap lateral margins and transtensional shear-dilation strain concentration, and (4) chemical geothermometry disequilibrium + 2 m thermal probe anomalies.
named_non_fault_mimic: (1) I-80/US-50 highway and railroad embankments across flat playas (damped via US Census TIGER/Line tiger_road_distance_m.tif); (2) historic open-pit and trench mining disturbances (controlled via BLM closed mining claim distance blm_closed_claim_distance_m.tif); (3) 3.5 km / 7.0 km rectilinear MT, GPS, and earthquake inversion grid cell boundaries (eliminated via sigma=36 px Gaussian spectral de-aliasing, IR-H77G-01); (4) Pleistocene Lake Lahontan (1332 m) & Bonneville (1463/1552 m) shoreline berms (controlled via equipotential shoreline bands + 1.6 km along-strike elevation variance).
